archetype.name: Play-In Team (offense-first)
archetype.definition: Miami has a top-ten offense and a bottom-ten defense, which nets out to a middle-of-the-league margin that its 10-6 record and seven-game win streak dress up.

report.headline: Seven straight wins, but a leaky defense and Giannis out cloud the picture
report.take:
On paper this is the most dangerous Miami offense in years and the least Miami-like defense. The Heat score 118 points per 100 possessions, 7th in the league, after five straight seasons with a mid-pack or worse offense. Their 120.69 points a game leads the league, though the 101.6 pace inflates that. They get there by shooting well and getting to the line: eFG % of 55.8 (5th), FT Rate of 32.6 (5th) and a low TOV % of 12.5 (8th). The defense allows 116.8 per 100 (23rd). That is a sharp break from a franchise that ranked 5th or 9th in defense in four of the previous five seasons.

The engine is the frontcourt, graded A. Giannis Antetokounmpo is first of 86 on the power-forward tab with 423 points, a 32.8 USG % and a BPM of 8.8. Bam Adebayo is 5th among centers at 62.5 TS %. The guards and wings are C+ around them. Davion Mitchell (138 assists, 63.5 TS %) and Klay Thompson (60 threes, 63.1 TS %) are efficient, but the depth is shaky: Tim Hardaway Jr. sits 107th of 108 shooting guards, with a 38.7 TS %. The sheet lists Antetokounmpo as Out, and that is the biggest fact on this card. He carries the usage, the efficiency and the A grade, and the sheet does not say for how long.

The record and the margin tell different stories. Miami is 10-6, but its point differential implies 9 wins, and its Net Rtg of 1.2 ranks exactly 15th. The hot streak is real but has context. The last five games were all at home and won by 13.4 points a game. The earlier road trip included lopsided losses at the Lakers and Golden State and an overtime escape against the Clippers. October was 2-4, November 8-2.

The defense's problem is specific. Opponents hit 38.3% from three (28th) and post a 56.2 eFG % (26th), yet Miami protects the rim well, with Opp Rim FG % of 62.3 (7th). Shooting guards have feasted, scoring 35.31 a game, the most allowed in the league. Some of that three-point damage is opponent shooting luck that should cool. Some of it is a perimeter group that cannot contain anyone. The truthful read is a fringe playoff team whose ceiling depends on one player's health.

strengths.title: Efficient, foul-drawing half-court offense
strengths.body: Miami's ORtg of 118 ranks 7th, built on shot quality and free throws rather than volume threes: eFG % ranks 5th and FT Rate 5th, while 3P % sits exactly at the league average. A low turnover rate helps, too. A shot profile like that holds up better than a hot-shooting spike, though losing Antetokounmpo's rim pressure will dent the free-throw rate.

strengths.title: A-grade frontcourt, Adebayo the constant
strengths.body: The frontcourt is the only group above C+. It accounts for most of the team's Win Shares and keeps the rim closed: opponents shoot 62.3% at the rim, 7th best. Adebayo, 5th among centers with a 4.3 BPM, is the piece that remains while Antetokounmpo is out, so the rim protection should hold even if the scoring dips.

strengths.title: Efficient secondary creators
strengths.body: Mitchell runs the offense at a 63.5 TS % with a positive on-off. Thompson has made 60 threes at a 63.1 TS %. Neither depends on high usage, which makes them the right players to absorb more possessions now. Whether their efficiency holds under a bigger load is the open question.

concerns.title: Antetokounmpo listed Out
concerns.body: He is the league's top power forward by the site's rankings, uses a third of the possessions he's on the floor for, and leads the team in points and rebounds. The A frontcourt grade and much of the offense's efficiency run through him. Portis, the next man at the position, has a 47.7 TS % and a -4 BPM.

concerns.title: Perimeter defense is bottom-five
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 38.3% from three, 28th in the league. Shooting guards score 35.31 a game against Miami, last in the league and well above what they average elsewhere. Some of the three-point damage should regress, since opponent 3P % is noisy. Still, the defensive rating of 23rd is a real drop from a franchise that sat 13th or better every recent season.

concerns.title: Margin trails the record
concerns.body: Ten wins on a differential worth 9 and a Net Rtg ranked 15th say this is a .500-plus team, not the 51-win pace the record projects. The guard depth behind Mitchell is thin as well: Larsson's on-off is -6.1, and Hardaway's -8.7 BPM is among the worst at his position.

trend.note: A 2-4 October gave way to an 8-2 November and seven straight wins, capped by a 5-0 home stand at +13.4 a game. Antetokounmpo's absence makes the next stretch a real test of whether the rise holds.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, two against top-ten teams, without Giannis
weekAhead.body:
The streak was built at home. This week is all road: Philadelphia, New York and Cleveland. The Sixers are 14-3, but their W vs Pt Diff of 4 is the league's highest, so their Net Rtg of 3.0 is closer to Miami's level than the record suggests. The Knicks are the hardest test, with the 4th-best defense, the 2nd-best REB % and a pace far slower than Miami's. They have also been stingiest in the league against power forwards relative to those players' usual output.

Cleveland is the friendliest matchup. Miami beat the Cavaliers 133-121 at home ten days ago. Cleveland's defense ranks 20th, it concedes heavily to shooting guards and centers, and its wings are graded D-. The danger is Cleveland's 37.1% three-point shooting against Miami's leaky perimeter. One win in three would be acceptable; two would say the team holds up without its star.

keyMatchups.title: Attacking Philadelphia at the rim
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia lets opponents take 35.6% of their shots at the rim, 29th, and concedes the most above-average scoring to power forwards. That would have been Antetokounmpo's night. Without him, Adebayo and the drivers have to take what's there, because the Sixers are stingy with centers and almost never turn it over.

keyMatchups.title: Knicks' glass and slow pace
keyMatchups.body: New York's defense holds teams to 108.4 per 100, and its 53.5 REB % ranks 2nd. Miami's offensive rebounding ranks 25th, so second chances will be scarce. The Knicks' 94.7 pace drags Miami away from its tempo, and their low free-throw rate limits a key Miami edge, the whistle.

keyMatchups.title: Guards against Cleveland's soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland gives shooting guards 30.76 points a game, 28th, and centers 22.24, 24th. That sets up Thompson and Adebayo. The flip side is Cleveland's 37.1% three-point shooting against Miami's 28th-ranked three-point defense.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the offense stays near 118 per 100 on the road with Antetokounmpo out, and who absorbs his possessions.

restOfSeason.body: The offense's foundations — shot quality, free throws, ball security — are sustainable, and an opponent three-point percentage near the bottom of the league should drift back somewhat, which helps the defense. But the margin says a team a little above .500. The 51-win pace comes from the record, not the play, and the close-game edge is small but on the wrong side of regression. The biggest variable is Antetokounmpo. With him healthy for most of the remaining 66 games, Miami's offense can stay top-ten and push into the mid-40s in wins. A long absence leaves a C+ perimeter and a defense ranked 23rd playing for play-in seeding.

confidence.note: Only 16 games, an injury of unknown length to the best player, and a streak built mostly at home.
